Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you to potential hypertension issues. However, they do not provide actual blood pressure readings.

A number of smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they need to be calibrated periodically with a traditional cuff-based blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide complete blood pressure measurements without the need for calibration, citing a trial involving thousands of participants to support the claim……

「Silent Killer」

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and low blood pressure (hypotension) can both pose significant health risks.

Of the two, hypertension is the more dangerous and has been dubbed the 「silent killer」 because it can cause serious, irreversible damage to the arteries, heart and brain without any obvious symptoms. The condition often only comes to light after triggering a heart attack or stroke.

Particularly for the elderly, regular blood pressure monitoring is a good idea, and there are home cuff-based blood pressure monitors available for self-measurement. Ideally, though, fully automated monitoring can be achieved through a fitness device you are already wearing.

Apple Watch Blood Pressure Feature

The launch of watchOS 26 has made it possible for five Apple Watch models to measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these devices will not give you any readings; instead, they issue alerts when signs of possible hypertension are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices can indeed provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require periodic calibration with cuff-based blood pressure monitor readings.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals claims to have successfully developed a smart ring that can achieve blood pressure measurements as accurate as a traditional upper-arm cuff monitor — without the need for calibration. This is the Signal Ring.

According to Bloomberg, the company's CEO Tom Moss said that he himself had nearly lost his life to undiagnosed high blood pressure, an experience that spurred him to found the company.

The ring will go on pre-order later today, ship in October and is priced at US$399 with no subscription required. Real-time blood pressure readings and long-term tracking data will be displayed in a companion app (see image above).

Worth noting is that the Signal Ring has not yet been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials have shown that the blood pressure readings it delivered on thousands of participants were remarkably accurate.

Interestingly, Moss does not intend to sell this ring to everyone — he says these professional features are best suited to the elderly, as well as people who have been told by a doctor that they are at risk of hypertension, implying that the Signal Ring may not be particularly outstanding in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
